name: TPS26600PWPR
title: TPS2660x: 60 V, 2 A industrial eFuse, protected against a reversed input
summary: A family of eFuses for 4.2 V to 60 V industrial rails, with two back-to-back N-channel FETs totalling 150 mΩ that block reverse current and survive a reversed input down to -60 V without extra parts. A resistor sets the current limit from 0.1 A to 2.23 A; a capacitor sets the output ramp; dividers set undervoltage and overvoltage levels, with internal 15 V and 33 V defaults. MODE picks current limiting or a timed circuit breaker, each latching or auto-retrying; IMON reports load current and FLT reports faults. TPS26600 and TPS26601 cut off on overvoltage; TPS26602 clamps the output at 38 V. TPS26600PWPR is the TPS26600 in 16-pin HTSSOP on a 2000-piece reel.
key_figures: 4.2 V to 60 V (62 V absolute max, -60 V reverse)
0.1 A to 2.23 A by R(ILIM); 0.95 to 1.05 A at 12 kΩ
1.19 V rising; internal 14.9 V and 32.6 V defaults
HTSSOP-16 5.0 mm × 4.4 mm; VQFN-24 5.0 mm × 4.0 mm
UL 2367 recognized, file 169910, R(ILIM) ≥ 5.36 kΩ (2.35 A max); UL60950 single-fault safe with open or shorted ILIM

notes: All ten are active, RoHS green with no Sb/Br, NiPdAu lead finish. The R suffix is the large reel, T the 250-piece reel. The TPS26601 comes only in VQFN. On VQFN parts the marking is on two lines, TPS over the device number.

circuits.title: 24 V, 1 A eFuse input protection for an industrial PLC CPU
circuits.description: TPS26600 between an 18 V to 30 V bus and a 2.2 mF load. One three-resistor string from IN to RTN feeds both comparators: R1/R2 junction to UVLO for an 18 V lockout, R2/R3 junction to OVP for a 30 V cut-off. R(ILIM) = 11.8 kΩ gives about 1 A, R(IMON) = 33.2 kΩ scales the monitor to 2.5 V at 1 A, and C(dVdT) = 2.2 µF stretches the ramp to about half a second so the inrush into C(OUT) stays near 0.1 A. MODE tied to RTN picks current limiting with auto-retry. FLT is pulled up to OUT through 100 kΩ.
notes: RTN and GND are separate nets; the bypass and output capacitors go to GND, the setting parts to RTN.

circuits.title: Active ORing of two supplies
circuits.description: Two TPS26600, each with its own UVLO/OVP divider, dVdT capacitor and current-limit resistor, feed one output bus and one load. Each device's reverse comparator blocks current back into the lower supply, so the pair acts as a low-drop diode OR. MODE ties to RTN on both. FLT, SHDN and IMON are left unconnected. No component values are given.
notes: On the unpowered device of the pair every control pin sits about 0.7 V from GND; its IMON and FLT readings are to be ignored.

circuits.title: Simple 24 V supply path protection
circuits.description: The fewest parts: C(IN), C(OUT) and R(ILIM). UVLO, OVP and MODE all go to RTN, so the device uses its internal 15 V lockout and 33 V cut-off and limits current with auto-retry; dVdT is left open for the 1.6 ms default ramp. FLT, SHDN and IMON are unconnected. Reverse input down to -60 V, reverse current and overcurrent are still covered.

parts.value: Input from a 24 V power supply

circuits.title: Implementation with optional transient protection parts
circuits.description: The full set of setting parts (UVLO/OVP divider R1 to R3, C(dVdT), R(ILIM), R(IMON), FLT pull-up R4 to OUT) plus two optional parts for surge: a bidirectional TVS from INPUT to GND and a Schottky diode from GND (anode) to OUTPUT (cathode) that catches the negative spike an inductive load or line throws when the switch opens. MODE ties to RTN; SHDN is unconnected. No component values are given.
notes: Where surge tests apply, at least 1 µF at the input keeps the input's falling slew within 20 V/µs.

operation.text: A 4.2 V to 60 V eFuse with two N-channel FETs back to back (150 mΩ total) that withstands ±60 V on its input. It controls inrush, limits current to ±5 % at 1 A, cuts off a short in 250 ns typical, watches the bus for undervoltage and overvoltage with ±3 % thresholds, blocks reverse current, reports faults and load current, and shuts down on overtemperature.

When UVLO falls below V(UVLOF) the FETs turn off quickly and FLT goes low; the comparator has 90 mV of hysteresis. A divider IN-UVLO-RTN sets the level. UVLO tied to RTN selects an internal 15 V level with 1 V hysteresis; tied to IN it disables the lockout; it must not float. A separate power-on reset on IN disables the circuit below V(PORF) (3.72 V), with 275 mV hysteresis.
OVP above V(OVPR) turns the FETs off. A divider IN-OVP-RTN sets the level (up to 55 V); OVP tied to RTN selects an internal 33 V level with 2 V hysteresis.
OVP is tied to RTN. Once the input passes 38 V the output is held at VOVC and the FET drops the difference, dissipating (VIN – VOVC) × IOUT; held long enough this ends in thermal shutdown.

Protection against a reversed supply is built in, so no series diode is needed; the device survives -60 V. It relies on RTN being separate from GND: joining RTN to GND removes the protection and a reversed input then destroys the device. Designs that need no reverse protection may join RTN, GND and the pad.

At turn-on a 4.7 µA source charges the dVdT capacitor and the output follows it with a gain of 24.6. Left open, dVdT gives about 23.9 V in 1.6 ms; a capacitor to RTN slows it. A 14 Ω switch discharges dVdT in shutdown.

With MODE to RTN (auto-retry) or 402 kΩ to RTN (latch-off), an overload is held at I(OL). FLT goes low after 875 µs. The output sags and dissipation rises until TJ reaches T(TSD) and the FETs turn off. Latch-off stays off until V(IN) falls below V(PORF) or SHDN is toggled; auto-retry restarts 512 ms after TJ drops 10 °C below T(TSD).
In current-limit operation FLT goes low once an overload lasts longer than tPGOODF (875 µs typical), ahead of the thermal shutdown that will follow, and stays low until the fault clears.

With MODE open, overload current passes as long as it stays below I(FASTRIP). A timer runs while the current is between I(CB) and I(FASTRIP); after tCB(dly) the FETs turn off and FLT goes low. TPS26600 and TPS26602 retry after 540 ms; TPS26601 latches off until V(IN) falls below V(PORF) or SHDN is toggled.

A fast-trip comparator at 1.87 × I(OL) + 0.015 A turns the FETs off within 250 ns typical, because the current-limit loop is too slow for a hard short. The FETs stay off for a few microseconds, then come back slowly with the loop regulating to I(OL), after which the overload behaviour applies. Starting into a short, the current is held at I(OL).

FLT pulls low on undervoltage, overvoltage, overload, reverse current, thermal shutdown, in shutdown (SHDN low), and during start-up until the FETs are fully enhanced, which lets it serve as a power-good signal. Faults are deglitched internally. V(IN) below V(PORF) resets it. With a reversed input, the FLT connection to downstream logic needs care.

IMON sources about 78 µA per amp of load current; a resistor to RTN makes a voltage, linear up to the lower of V(IN) – 1.5 V and 4 V. With a reversed input, a 100 kΩ series resistor between IMON and an ADC limits current into the ADC's ESD structures.
Above T(TSD) (157 °C typical) the FETs turn off and FLT goes low. Depending on MODE the device then stays off or retries 512 ms after TJ falls below T(TSD) – 10 °C.

Pulling SHDN below 0.76 V, from a GPIO or an opto-isolator, turns the FETs off and cuts quiescent current to 20 µA typical. Whatever pulls it low has to take 10 µA or more while holding 400 mV; releasing it above 1 V re-enables the device, which restarts through the dVdT ramp.

operation.topic: Choosing C(IN) and the FLT pull-up
operation.text: The FLT pull-up is typically 10 kΩ to 100 kΩ, keeping FLT's sink current under 10 mA. C(IN) is a local ceramic of typically 0.1 µF to 1 µF; above 0.1 µF if the source is more than a few inches away. The supply must be able to deliver more than the current limit.

Start-up dissipation is often an order of magnitude above steady state. Pick the ramp time so that the start-up dissipation, with and without load, stays inside the thermal shutdown time curve with margin; a larger C(dVdT) lowers it.

When the switch interrupts current, inductance in the input lead raises a positive spike at IN and inductance in the output lead a negative spike at OUT. Short leads, a large ground plane, a Schottky diode across the output, about 0.1 µF of ceramic at the input, and where needed a TVS keep them within the absolute maximum ratings.

A 0.1 µF or larger ceramic from IN to GND, as close as possible, with a small loop. Power path traces short and sized for at least twice the full-load current. RTN is a copper plane or island. Setting parts sit next to their pins and return to RTN by the shortest trace; the R(ILIM) and R(IMON) traces stay short and away from switching signals. Protection parts sit close to what they protect; the output Schottky close to OUT and GND. The pad is soldered to the RTN plane under the device, with other layers adding heat spreading.
